bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh signals September rate hike; BofA sees three hikes this year
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is reportedly prepared to support a September rate hike per FT, with markets now pricing ~70% probability of at least one hike this year. Bank of America has revised its outlook to expect three rate hikes total. Separately, critics note Warsh's stated goal of eliminating forward guidance is being undercut by colleagues leaking policy speculation to the FT, damaging Fed credibility.

bullets.title: U.S. labor data strong: jobless claims 199K, productivity beats at +1.4% QoQ
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 199K (est. 205K), remaining near 57-year lows for a third consecutive week. Q2 nonfarm productivity rose 1.4% vs. 0.6% consensus, while unit labor costs came in at 1.3% vs. 2.1% forecast — a broadly disinflationary labor print that nonetheless supports a hawkish Fed pivot.

bullets.title: Tom Lee targets S&P 500 8,000 in August; record call option volume confirms bullish positioning
bullets.body: Fundstrat's Tom Lee sees the S&P 500 hitting 7,900–8,000 in August, citing technical momentum, broadening market breadth, and accelerating earnings. S&P 500 call option volume hit a record 4M+ contracts on Tuesday, and Kalshi prediction markets assign 66.9% probability to the index reaching 8,000 in 2026; the index is currently ~3.6% below that level. A $2.7B SPY call wall sits at 775.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz geopolitical crisis escalates: Iran proposes transit controls, US/Israel vessels reportedly banned
bullets.body: Iran's parliament is reviewing a draft bill to restrict Hormuz transit, with Iranian state media FARS reporting US and Israeli vessels are prohibited under a potential Iran-Oman framework deal. The US has affirmed Hormuz is an international waterway and that no single party controls the lanes, but traffic data shows only 3 outbound/0 inbound vessels on 8/5. Brent crude jumped above $82/bbl on the news, and European gas prices surged 5.7% to €55.39/MWh.

bullets.title: Yardeni calls for hawkish Fed pivot; Warsh's Trump ties and anti-guidance stance in focus
bullets.body: Yardeni Research argues the Fed should turn more hawkish, citing consumer spending up 3.3%, business investment up 8.4%, and AI-driven capex supporting growth. Bloomberg reports Trump has held regular calls with Fed Chair Warsh since May discussing the economy, though no direct policy direction is reported. Warsh's push to eliminate forward guidance faces internal resistance from colleagues speculating to media about upcoming meetings.

bullets.title: U.S. crude inventories at 40-year lows; Saudi imports hit zero for first time since 1985
bullets.body: US crude oil inventories have fallen for a record 17 consecutive weeks to their lowest level since March 1984. US imports of Saudi crude fell to zero in July — the first full month at zero since 1985 — as Gulf supply disruptions forced refiners to seek alternatives including Venezuela. Fitch forecasts Brent returning to oversupply from September and targeting $70/bbl by Q4 2026.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler bond issuance surges: GOOGL raises $25B with $115B demand; AMZN/META at $170B YTD
bullets.body: Alphabet launched a $25B investment-grade bond offering across up to 10 tranches (2–40yr maturities) and drew ~$115B in investor demand, widening hyperscaler credit spreads. Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta have collectively sold nearly $170B in IG bonds YTD 2026, dwarfing prior year tech issuance. Morgan Stanley projects global cloud capex to hit $1.2T by 2027, up from ~1.4% of GDP in 2025 to ~3% by 2027–2029.

bullets.title: NVIDIA weighing HBM reduction in Rubin Ultra GPU amid advanced memory shortage
bullets.body: The Information reports NVIDIA is considering using less high-bandwidth memory in its upcoming Rubin Ultra GPU design to address a severe HBM chip shortage. The move would be a negative for HBM suppliers (SK hynix, Samsung, Micron) and reflects ongoing DRAM/HBM supply constraints. South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.6% on the news, with SK hynix -10.4% and Samsung -6.3%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor test cycle inflection confirmed: Advantest raises 2026 TAM, OSAT capex at all-time highs
bullets.body: Advantest revised its 2026 memory TAM estimate up 12% to $2.75B and SoC TAM up 21% to $11B. Q2 test capex at major OSATs hit an all-time high at nearly 2x the prior peak, with monthly tester installs at record levels. Teradyne notes test equipment is now growing faster than fab equipment after a decade of underperformance, with memory book-to-bill exceeding 2.

bullets.title: Tesla Terafab: 1TW compute target, DRAM hiring, chip demand signals major semiconductor tailwind
bullets.body: Tesla announced Terafab will be built in Grimes County, Texas, targeting over 1 terawatt of compute output per year. The company is actively hiring memory process engineers for DRAM production, and Elon Musk estimates ~25% of Terafab compute will serve Tesla Optimus, ~75% for AI/spacecraft. Tesla and SpaceX stated they will need far more chips than current global production can supply.

bullets.title: Retail traders rotating defensive; 'FOMO to Oh No' sentiment shift underway
bullets.body: Retail traders are flipping from momentum-chasing FOMO positioning to defensive allocations amid macro uncertainty. Simultaneously, record S&P 500 call option volumes and bullish Kalshi market pricing suggest institutional/options market participants remain constructive — a divergence between retail sentiment and derivatives positioning.

bullets.title: Eurozone EPS revisions outpacing U.S. for first time since January 2025
bullets.body: Eurozone EPS revisions have risen for 17 consecutive weeks and are now above U.S. EPS revision levels for the first time since January 2025, suggesting a potential rotation opportunity into European equities relative to U.S.

bullets.title: Yardeni/Bessent: K-shaped economy 'definitively over'; US capturing more global profit share
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent declared the K-shaped economy is 'definitively over,' signaling a macro view that divergence between high- and low-income outcomes is closing. Separately, data shows the U.S. is capturing an ever-greater share of global corporate profits, while Visa research notes Gen X and millennials have built more wealth than boomers at comparable ages.

bullets.title: U.S. pending home sales hit 5-month low; mortgage rates still pressuring buyers
bullets.body: Pending home sales fell 3.7% week-over-week and 1.9% year-over-year to 311,150 units, the lowest level in over five months. Elevated mortgage rates are cited as the primary driver of buyer pullback, consistent with the broader rate-hike expectations now being priced in by markets.

bullets.title: Copper at record highs on data center demand and Congo supply disruption
bullets.body: Copper hit a new record high driven by strong global demand — particularly from data center construction — and supply tightness compounded by DR Congo export disruptions. One data center rack manufacturer reported a 2.5-year order backlog as of February 2026. Since October, copper is up 40% while the Mag7 is roughly flat.

bullets.title: Google warns of sophisticated ransomware campaign targeting Wall Street firms
bullets.body: Google flagged a ransomware hacking campaign targeting over two dozen major U.S. financial institutions including Blackstone, Moody's, and CME via phone-based social engineering to steal employee credentials and create fake IT helpdesk sites.

bullets.title: WDC -21%, SNDK -13% on session; Jefferies cuts SNDK PT 42% to $1,750
bullets.body: Western Digital and SanDisk are seeing sharp selloffs, with WDC down 21% and SNDK down 13% on the session. Jefferies cut its SNDK price target from $3,000 to $1,750 (a 42% reduction) while maintaining a Buy rating, reflecting deteriorating memory sector sentiment tied to the NVDA HBM reduction report and Korean market weakness.

bullets.title: PCE inflation methodology change starting August could reduce reported inflation readings
bullets.body: Senator Elizabeth Warren is seeking details on new PCE inflation methodology changes taking effect with August data (released in September), which could mechanically reduce reported inflation figures and complicate Fed policy interpretation.

bullets.title: Japan's second-largest ever yen intervention ($85B) adds liquidity; yen weakens past 158
bullets.body: Japan conducted its second-largest currency intervention on record at $85B last week, second only to the Fukushima-era support. Despite the intervention, USD/JPY has weakened back beyond 158 — its weakest level in nearly a week — with critics questioning intervention effectiveness. The joint U.S.-Japan support mechanism is described as unusual and adds liquidity to already-flush U.S. markets.

bullets.title: AI semiconductor July 2026 drawdown: worst month since 2002, $1T+ market cap wiped
bullets.body: July 2026 was characterized as the sharpest drawdown of the AI cycle, with semiconductors posting their worst month since 2002 and over $1 trillion in AI-linked market value declining. The key debate centers on compute as the deepest moat in LLM competition and whether the memory supercycle thesis remains intact as names like NVDA, AMD, and others attempt to recover.
